ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the middle of the figure is a regular hexagon, and a square is connected to the outside of each of the six sides; between each two adjacent squares there is a triangle, for a total of six triangles. The outer contour is composed of several line segments, and can be regarded as each square contributing one exposed side, and each triangle between adjacent squares contributing one exposed base side. Reasoning: The problem gives that the side length of the regular hexagon is 1. Each square is built on one side of the regular hexagon, so the side length of each square is also 1. Each interior angle of a regular hexagon is 120°, and the angle formed between two adjacent externally attached squares is 60°, so the triangle sandwiched between them is an equilateral triangle with side length 1, and therefore the exposed base side of the triangle also has length 1. Around the outside there are altogether 6 exposed sides of squares and 6 exposed sides of triangles, each of length 1, so the perimeter is 6×1+6×1=12.

raw_record.question_text: The diagram shows a shape made from a regular hexagon of side one unit, six triangles and six squares. What is the perimeter of the shape?

method.method_draft: Direct boundary-count method: First describe the image as a central regular hexagon with one square attached to each of its six sides, and six triangular gaps between adjacent squares; the visible outer outline alternates between one exposed side of a square and one exposed base of a triangle. From the text, take the central hexagon side length as 1 unit. Since each square is built on a side of the hexagon, every square side is 1. At each hexagon vertex, the two adjacent square sides form a 60-degree angle because the regular hexagon has interior angle 120 degrees and the squares turn outward; hence each intervening triangle is equilateral with side 1, so its exposed base is also 1. Count the 12 exposed outer segments: 6 square sides plus 6 triangle bases. Therefore the perimeter is 12 units.

method.method_draft: Composite-perimeter subtraction method: From the image, identify all component adjacencies: six unit squares each share one side with the central hexagon, and each of the six triangles lies between two neighboring squares, sharing two of its sides with those squares. From the text, the regular hexagon has side 1, so each attached square has side 1. Using the same regular-hexagon angle relationship, the triangles are equilateral unit triangles. Add the perimeters of all separate pieces: central hexagon contributes 6, six squares contribute 6×4=24, and six triangles contribute 6×3=18, for a total of 48. Then subtract twice every internal shared unit edge. There are 6 hexagon-square shared edges and 12 square-triangle shared edges, so subtract 2×18=36. The remaining outer perimeter is 48−36=12.
